front: What is the practical difference between EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE in PostgreSQL?
back: EXPLAIN shows the planner's estimated execution plan, while EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually runs the statement and reports observed timing and row counts, making estimate errors visible.
accepted_answers: EXPLAIN shows the planner's estimated execution plan, while EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually runs the statement and reports observed timing and row counts, making estimate errors visible.
hint: One predicts; the other executes and measures.

front: Why can a sequential scan be the correct PostgreSQL plan even when an index exists?
back: If a query returns a large fraction of a table or the table is small, reading pages sequentially can be cheaper than many index lookups plus heap fetches.
accepted_answers: If a query returns a large fraction of a table or the table is small, reading pages sequentially can be cheaper than many index lookups plus heap fetches.
hint: An index is not automatically cheaper for broad result sets.

front: How does column order matter in a multicolumn B-tree index?
back: The leading columns determine which predicates can efficiently narrow the index range; choose order based on real equality and range predicates and workload rather than a blanket selectivity rule.
accepted_answers: The leading columns determine which predicates can efficiently narrow the index range; choose order based on real equality and range predicates and workload rather than a blanket selectivity rule.
hint: Think leftmost usable prefix and actual query shapes.

front: What is a partial index and when is it useful?
back: A partial index stores only rows matching a predicate, reducing index size and maintenance cost when queries repeatedly target a stable subset such as active or unprocessed rows.
accepted_answers: A partial index stores only rows matching a predicate, reducing index size and maintenance cost when queries repeatedly target a stable subset such as active or unprocessed rows.
hint: Index only the hot subset the workload repeatedly filters on.

front: What is an expression index?
back: An expression index indexes the result of an expression such as lower(email), allowing queries using that same expression to use an index efficiently.
accepted_answers: An expression index indexes the result of an expression such as lower(email), allowing queries using that same expression to use an index efficiently.
hint: The indexed value can be computed rather than a raw column.

front: What does INCLUDE provide in a PostgreSQL B-tree index?
back: INCLUDE stores non-key columns in the index so an index-only scan may satisfy a query without making those columns part of the search ordering.
accepted_answers: INCLUDE stores non-key columns in the index so an index-only scan may satisfy a query without making those columns part of the search ordering.
hint: Cover selected columns without changing key semantics.

front: Why can low-selectivity indexes be poor candidates for some queries?
back: When a predicate matches many rows, the index may require many random heap accesses and provide little filtering, so PostgreSQL may prefer a sequential scan.
accepted_answers: When a predicate matches many rows, the index may require many random heap accesses and provide little filtering, so PostgreSQL may prefer a sequential scan.
hint: An index helps most when it meaningfully reduces work.

front: What problem does MVCC solve in PostgreSQL?
back: MVCC lets readers observe a consistent snapshot while writers create new row versions, reducing reader-writer blocking while preserving transactional visibility rules.
accepted_answers: MVCC lets readers observe a consistent snapshot while writers create new row versions, reducing reader-writer blocking while preserving transactional visibility rules.
hint: Readers use snapshots instead of locking every row they inspect.

front: Why are VACUUM and autovacuum essential in PostgreSQL?
back: Updates and deletes leave dead row versions under MVCC; vacuum reclaims reusable space, maintains visibility information, and prevents transaction-ID wraparound problems.
accepted_answers: Updates and deletes leave dead row versions under MVCC; vacuum reclaims reusable space, maintains visibility information, and prevents transaction-ID wraparound problems.
hint: Dead tuples do not disappear immediately when rows change.

front: What is table or index bloat?
back: Bloat is excess storage occupied by obsolete or poorly reused tuples and pages, increasing I/O and cache pressure even though the logical data set is smaller.
accepted_answers: Bloat is excess storage occupied by obsolete or poorly reused tuples and pages, increasing I/O and cache pressure even though the logical data set is smaller.
hint: Physical size can grow faster than useful data.

front: What is a HOT update in PostgreSQL?
back: A Heap-Only Tuple update can avoid creating new index entries when indexed columns are unchanged and there is suitable page space, reducing write amplification.
accepted_answers: A Heap-Only Tuple update can avoid creating new index entries when indexed columns are unchanged and there is suitable page space, reducing write amplification.
hint: No indexed column change can allow a cheaper heap-local update.

front: Under PostgreSQL Read Committed, can two SELECT statements in one transaction see different committed data?
back: Yes. Each statement gets a snapshot as the statement begins, so a later statement can observe changes committed by other transactions in between.
accepted_answers: Yes. Each statement gets a snapshot as the statement begins, so a later statement can observe changes committed by other transactions in between.
hint: Read Committed uses statement-level snapshots.

front: What must an application be prepared to do when using PostgreSQL Serializable isolation?
back: It must be prepared to retry transactions that PostgreSQL aborts with a serialization failure because the database protects serializable behavior by rejecting unsafe concurrent executions.
accepted_answers: It must be prepared to retry transactions that PostgreSQL aborts with a serialization failure because the database protects serializable behavior by rejecting unsafe concurrent executions.
hint: Serializable correctness may surface as retryable aborts.

front: What is the first thing to inspect when a PostgreSQL query is unexpectedly slow?
back: Inspect its actual execution plan and runtime evidence, ideally with EXPLAIN ANALYZE plus buffers where safe, before guessing at indexes or configuration changes.
accepted_answers: Inspect its actual execution plan and runtime evidence, ideally with EXPLAIN ANALYZE plus buffers where safe, before guessing at indexes or configuration changes.
hint: Measure the plan before tuning.

front: What is pg_stat_statements useful for?
back: It aggregates execution statistics by normalized SQL, helping identify high-total-time, high-frequency, or slow query families that deserve tuning.
accepted_answers: It aggregates execution statistics by normalized SQL, helping identify high-total-time, high-frequency, or slow query families that deserve tuning.
hint: Find expensive query patterns across many executions.

front: What is the main value of jOOQ's generated code?
back: jOOQ generates Java types from the database schema, giving SQL-oriented queries compile-time awareness of tables, columns, and types instead of relying on stringly typed SQL construction.
accepted_answers: jOOQ generates Java types from the database schema, giving SQL-oriented queries compile-time awareness of tables, columns, and types instead of relying on stringly typed SQL construction.
hint: Think schema-derived type safety while staying close to SQL.

front: Why should jOOQ code still use bind values instead of concatenating user input?
back: Bind values separate data from SQL syntax, reduce injection risk, preserve type handling, and can improve plan reuse; jOOQ's fluent API does not remove the need for safe parameterization.
accepted_answers: Bind values separate data from SQL syntax, reduce injection risk, preserve type handling, and can improve plan reuse; jOOQ's fluent API does not remove the need for safe parameterization.
hint: A fluent DSL is not a license to interpolate untrusted strings.

front: Why should a jOOQ transaction scope be kept around the business invariant rather than around remote calls?
back: Keeping a database transaction open across slow network calls extends lock and snapshot lifetimes, increases contention, and makes failures harder to recover from; keep DB work focused and coordinate external effects explicitly.
accepted_answers: Keeping a database transaction open across slow network calls extends lock and snapshot lifetimes, increases contention, and makes failures harder to recover from; keep DB work focused and coordinate external effects explicitly.
hint: Long external waits are expensive inside a database transaction.

front: Why must Flyway migrations and jOOQ generated classes stay synchronized?
back: The runtime schema and generated Java model must represent the same contract; schema changes without regenerated code can cause compile-time or runtime drift, while generated code without deployed migration targets columns that do not exist.
accepted_answers: The runtime schema and generated Java model must represent the same contract; schema changes without regenerated code can cause compile-time or runtime drift, while generated code without deployed migration targets columns that do not exist.
hint: Schema-first type safety depends on code generation matching migrations.

front: What is a common N+1 problem even in SQL-first application code?
back: Fetching a parent list and then issuing one child query per parent multiplies round trips; prefer an appropriate join, nested result construction, or batched follow-up when the result shape permits it.
accepted_answers: Fetching a parent list and then issuing one child query per parent multiplies round trips; prefer an appropriate join, nested result construction, or batched follow-up when the result shape permits it.
hint: Count database round trips, not just individual query speed.
